Patrick J. Owens profiled Stewart Rawlings Mott for the Detroit Free Press and Detroit Magazine on January 19, 1969. Mott was 30 years old and already famous as a political philanthropist. In a single election year he had given 365,000 dollars to politicians. The profile's title calls that 'One Man's Fortune.'

Mott's money came from a family fortune tied to General Motors. He spent it on candidates and causes, many of them liberal, at a scale few donors matched. Owens presents the man behind the checks: his style, his causes, and the attention his giving bought. The profile captures a new kind of political figure, the heir as donor, at the moment he became news.
